objective.primary: Make ARWP an inspectable primary source about agentic-web interoperability that AI/search systems can identify, retrieve, verify and cite without relying on marketing claims or opaque readiness scores.
targetQuestions: What is an agentic web resolver?
How can an AI agent discover what interfaces a website exposes?
What is the difference between MCP, A2A, WebMCP and llms.txt?
Which agent-facing discovery mechanisms are used on the web today?
How should a website expose multilingual discovery surfaces to AI agents?
What evidence supports an ARWP resolver decision?

sitemap.notes: Planned explicit project sitemap; do not treat the URL as observed until deployed.

robots.notes: Planned explicit crawler policy surface for the project path.

answerPages.description: Create concise canonical pages for recurring agentic-web questions, with direct answers, evidence and stable source URLs.

originalResearch.description: Publish reviewed resolver benchmarks, negative results and future State of the Agentic Web measurements as original evidence rather than generic SEO content.

protocolObservatory.description: Maintain a dated protocol observatory covering MCP, A2A, WebMCP, llms.txt, Agent Skills, commerce protocols and other relevant discovery surfaces.

comparisonPages.description: Publish source-backed comparison pages such as MCP vs A2A, WebMCP vs MCP and llms.txt vs agent manifests.

conceptDefinitions.description: Publish canonical definitions for ARWP concepts including agentic web resolver, capability graph, resolver regret and discovery conflict.

claimsRegistry.description: Assign stable identifiers to important technical claims and expose status, review date, evidence and machine-readable representations.

evidenceReceipts.description: Turn resolver observations and benchmark claims into durable replayable evidence receipts with digests and provenance.

crawlerMatrix.description: Maintain a dated matrix of AI/search crawler roles, official documentation, robots behavior and recommended configuration without inferring unsupported behavior.

agentFetchLab.description: Run reproducible experiments measuring which web surfaces agents actually fetch first for concrete tasks instead of assuming special files are always used.

knowledgeGraph.description: Link protocols, concepts, claims, evidence and project surfaces in a machine-readable entity relationship graph.

citationVisuals.description: Publish reusable research charts and diagrams with source notes, accessible alt text, stable URLs and explicit reuse terms.

openReuseAssets.description: Publish a permission-free press/media pack under CC BY 4.0 with machine-readable reuse rights, canonical press facts, attribution guidance and explicit AI/ML training, indexing, embedding and RAG reuse permission for covered materials.

externalDistribution.description: Turn each substantial research release into externally distributed references while keeping the ARWP canonical URL and evidence as the source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Measure observable citations, grounding queries, referrals, external mentions and referring domains without collapsing them into a single score.

localization.description: Expose English canonical semantics plus reviewed German and Russian discovery routing for AI agents with deterministic English fallback.

history.description: Expose product evolution, releases, maturity and current status as both a human timeline and machine-readable JSON.

vocabulary.definition: Software that discovers multiple machine- and agent-facing interfaces exposed by a website, preserves their provenance, reports conflicts and selects an interface for a concrete intent.
A decision-quality case where a simpler discovery strategy selects the reviewed-correct interface while the union Resolver selects an incorrect one.
A visible disagreement between independently observed or publisher-declared discovery sources that a resolver must preserve rather than silently overwrite.

signals.name: search visibility
signals.description: Track canonical page indexing, search queries and search performance using available webmaster tooling.

signals.name: AI citations and referrals
signals.description: Track observable AI citations, grounding queries, referrals and external mentions where platforms expose them.

signals.name: referring domains
signals.description: Track external sources that cite or link to ARWP research, definitions, evidence and visual assets.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate, privacy-minimized visibility signals; do not collect resolver inputs or visitor activity into a browsing-history dataset.
